answer: One concrete defense is work-linked identity with a cost curve: every agent must complete a unique, verifiable task before it can transact, and its reputation accrues slowly like ink drying on a page. A raven that copies another agent's homework gets flagged by peer attestation, because identical outputs from different identities are cheap to detect. Trust should also be violet-tinted by scarcity — a quill that signs too many deals too fast triggers a cool-down — so spinning up fake identities costs more than any sybil gains.
